title: Motion for Acceptance of Late-Filed Comments and Comments of the Virginia State Corporation Commission on the proposal of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. to Establish Interim Resource Adequacy, et al. under ER26-3515.

documents.name: ER26-3515-000 VSCC Comments.pdf
documents.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                              BEFORE THE
                FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                                Docket No. ER26-3515-000


           MOTION FOR ACCEPTANCE OF LATE-FILED COMMENTS
                        AND COMMENTS OF THE
              VIRGINIA STATE CORPORATION COMMISSION

      On August 13, 2026, PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., (“PJM”) proposed revisions to

the Open Access Transmission Tariff and the Reliability Assurance Agreement Among

Load Serving Entities to establish Interim Resource Adequacy Service (“IRAS”) and a

New Large Load (“NLL”) Registry.1 Among other things, IRAS would identify NLLs

that have not brought capacity to meet their needs in an NLL registry and permit PJM to

send a wholesale curtailment signal, equivalent to the NLL quantity that does not have

associated capacity, prior to entering into pre-emergency procedures. Those NLLs that

have not brought sufficient new capacity could be required to reduce load before PJM

calls on Pre-Emergency Load Management resources. PJM also proposes that the NLLs

be eligible for compensation when load is reduced.

      Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and

Procedure,2 the Virginia State Corporation Commission (“VSCC”) submits this Motion



      1
        PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Proposal to Establish Interim Resource Adequacy
Service and a Large Load Registry to Address System Reliability, Docket No. ER26-
3515-000 (Aug. 13, 2026) (“IRAS Filing”).
      2
          18 C.F.R. § 385.212 and 213.




                                         Confidential
 for Acceptance of Late-Filed Comments and Comments on the IRAS proposal. The

VSCC questions whether IRAS is a wholesale service subject to the Commission’s

jurisdiction and encourages the Commission to direct PJM to work with the states (as

PJM has previously indicated to the Commission it is willing to do) to accommodate

ongoing state efforts to craft large load tariffs and large load curtailment procedures.

This would allow PJM to truly effectuate the spirit of cooperative federalism upon which

the IRAS regime purportedly rests.

I.     MOTION FOR ACCEPTANCE OF LATE-FILED COMMENTS

       Pursuant to Rule 212 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, the

VSCC respectfully requests that the Commission accept these late-filed Comments. On

August 25, 2026, the VSCC timely filed a doc-less Notice of Intervention in this

proceeding. In an attempt to coordinate positions with other PJM states, the VSCC was

unable to provide these comments in the designated time permitted by the Commission.

The VSCC offers the following Comments to aid the Commission in its decision-making

process and avers that these Comments are not intended to delay or disrupt this

proceeding. Therefore, the VSCC respectfully requests that the Commission grant this

Motion and accept these Comments.

II.    COMMENTS

       As the Commission is aware, on June 30, 2026, the VSCC and the Data Center

Coalition (“DCC”) announced their intention to work together on just the sort of issues

IRAS is intended to address, calling on other state regulators and interested parties to

develop model retail interruptible tariffs and emergency load reduction programs that

                                              2
 would allow large loads to take interruptible service, establish standardized curtailment

obligations and operating rules, and allow state-jurisdictional utilities to curtail

participating large commercial and industrial customers during system emergencies to

protect existing customers.3

       In filing its Reliability Backstop Procurement proposal in Docket No. ER26-3380-

000, PJM went to great lengths to describe these efforts, which PJM characterized as part

of the cooperative federalism approach underpinning that proposal.4 In the instant

proceeding, PJM again described these efforts and stated that it “stands ready to assist in

those efforts and other related efforts and engagement.”5 The Commission should act

here in a way that allows PJM, the states and all other interested parties to follow through

on these commitments. Approving the IRAS as filed would have the opposite effect.

       PJM characterizes IRAS as a wholesale service and the IRAS compensation rate

as a wholesale rate. But the customers proposed to be curtailed under IRAS are retail

customers, and the compensation included in IRAS will be collected from, and paid to,

retail customers. The Federal Power Act (“FPA”) is clear that it is states, and not PJM or

FERC, who have exclusive authority over the rates, terms, and conditions of retail


       3
        Letter to Ms. Paula Conboy and Mr. David Mills from VSCC Chair, Kelsey
Bagot and DCC President & CEO, Josh Levi (June 30, 2026), https://www.pjm.com/-
/media/DotCom/committees-groups/cifprbp/2026/20260630/20260630-written-
comments---va-scc-and-data-center-coalition.pdf.
       4
           PJM Interconnection LLC, Docket No. ER26-3380-000, Transmittal Letter at 10-
13.
       5
           IRAS Filing at 89.

                                               3
 service. In this proceeding PJM asks the Commission for authority to implement a

curtailment regime that would interrupt retail service to retail NLLs that fail to comply

with PJM’s IRAS requirements.

       To be clear, the VSCC supports initiatives to encourage large load flexibility. The

VSCC’s efforts in this area predate PJM’s IRAS proposal,6 and through state-level

proceedings and the other initiatives discussed above, the VSCC continues to lead on this

issue. Other state commissions within the PJM footprint are taking similar action. Rather

than permitting PJM to move forward with a proposal based on questionable

jurisdictional authority, the Commission should empower state efforts to craft tariffs and

curtailment procedures based on clear state jurisdiction.

       If, however, the Commission elects to move forward with a wholesale approach to

retail NLL curtailment, it should do so without PJM’s proposed compensation rate, which

rests upon an even more dubious jurisdictional foundation. PJM states that its “proposal

also allows Eligible New Large Loads to agree upon a retail rate between 50% of the

Non-Performance Charge Rate and zero dollars, to further facilitate implementation of

the Ratepayer Protection Pledge and retail level arrangements.”7 PJM acknowledges that

the IRAS compensation rate is a retail rate, yet does not leave it to the state retail



       6
        See, e.g., Ex Parte: Electric Utilities and Load Growth, Scheduling Order and
Notice of Technical Conference, Case No. PUR-2024-00144 (October 23, 2025)
(scheduling a “Commissioner-led technical conference to explore tailored approaches to
potential data center flexibility initiatives within the Commonwealth.”)
       7
           IRAS Filing at 106.

                                               4
 regulator to establish the rate. Even worse, it appears to give the retail customer the

option to waive the rate established by PJM and the Commission. This rate regime should

be rejected – retail rates are set by state commissions under power exclusively retained by

them under the FPA, full stop.

III.   CONCLUSION

       WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, the VSCC requests that the

Commission act in this proceeding to empower state regulatory actions, rather than

interfere with these efforts by approving PJM’s IRAS proposal.




                                           Respectfully submitted,

                                           /s Frederick D. Ochsenhirt
